source_text.body:
Have Muse review what it knows and report back
A user asks Muse to review its context, take care of things, and report what it did; commenters suggest the goal feature and cron jobs to run it on a schedule.
·
Nov 1, 2026
Done with
MM
Meta Muse
What they did
The poster says they gave Muse access to routines, bills, inbox, calendar, Marketplace listings, and notes, then set up recurring jobs to check inbox, bills, calendar, and listings. They also run a weekly pass where Muse reviews its own notes, flags stale or contradictory information, fixes what it can, and sends a report on what it did or thinks should be added; commenters say the key is giving it scheduled jobs, clear reporting instructions, and limits on actions that need approval.
How it went
The thread reports qualitative results, not hard metrics: people say scheduled checks, drafts, morning or weekly reports, and goals/cron-style jobs made Muse more proactive. It also shows the main limit: users keep unsupervised work to read-only review, summaries, and drafts, while payments, sending, posting, deleting, or other irreversible steps still need human approval.
Worth knowing
Useful catch: one commenter recommends starting with one small recurring job and only expanding after it runs correctly twice.
Try it yourself
with
Meta Muse
Copy prompt
Review everything you currently know about my work and projects, including [areas, e.g. open tasks, upcoming deadlines, recent conversations]. Take care of what you safely can, then report back with what you did, what's still open, and what you need from me. Set this up to run on a schedule of [e.g. every morning], and ask me before sending anything externally or deleting anything.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/MuseAgent/comments/1xlknr8/how_do_you_get_muse_to_stop_waiting_around_and
